comparison: Perfect alignment on C85-C86. Both acknowledge study limitations (single donor-acceptor pair, lack of observed cooperativity) as reasonable constraints that don't undermine main conclusions. OpenEval notes these as appropriate acknowledgments; peer reviewers accepted them without dispute.

Strong agreement on C31-C40 validation experiments in SthKCterm. OpenEval finds the heterotetrameric design sound with consistent FRET measurements. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the data quality and the ability to extract distance distributions, stating 'data are excellent and convincingly support conclusions.' Both also cover C42-C50 validation claims with peer review affirming the quantitative analysis.

Both address C42-C50 validation of TCSPC approach. OpenEval emphasizes good fit quality, consistency with frequency-domain measurements, and agreement with structural predictions. Peer reviewers affirmed these findings as part of their broader endorsement of the validation experiments and quantitative methodology.

Agreement on C51-C55 intersubunit FRET findings. OpenEval finds the experimental design appropriate and results aligned with predictions. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns and praised the 'compelling quantitative analysis,' encompassing these intersubunit measurements within their overall endorsement.

Both address C81-C82 regarding intersubunit FRET methodology and limitations. OpenEval views the single additional acceptor simplification as reasonable given good fit quality while noting the limitation. Peer reviewers accepted this approach without concern as part of their affirmation of the methodological rigor.

Both cover C59 on distance parameter similarity between constructs. OpenEval finds this validates that homotetrameric constructs report similar conformational states despite intersubunit FRET. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this within their broader endorsement of the intersubunit FRET analysis.

Agreement on C63-C65, C69 regarding full-length channel measurements. OpenEval finds cAMP-dependent lifetime changes follow expected trends and appropriately notes caution about absolute KD values. Peer reviewers affirmed these findings, with one explicitly supporting that 'coupling of CNBDs to the rest of the channel stabilizes CNBDs in their active state.'

Both address C60-C62 protein quality control. OpenEval finds multiple orthogonal methods confirm successful preparation with minor truncation unlikely to affect measurements. Peer reviewers affirmed the full-length channel work without raising concerns about protein quality.

Strong agreement on C73-C76 energetic findings. OpenEval finds calculations well-defined using Boltzmann relationships, with similar ΔΔG values supporting modular gating. Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed this central finding, with editor stating study 'demonstrates that transmembrane domains stabilize CNBDs in their active state.'

Agreement on C77, C79-C80 regarding domain coupling nature. OpenEval finds consistency of distances validates structural similarity while cAMP-independent coupling provides mechanistic insight. Peer reviewers affirmed these conclusions as part of their endorsement of the energetic analysis and allosteric coupling findings.

Both address C83 allosteric interpretation. OpenEval finds interpretation consistent with data showing more favorable CNBD activation when pore is present. Peer reviewers accepted this mechanistic interpretation within their broader affirmation of the energetic findings.

Agreement on C84 comparison to HCN channels. OpenEval finds the comparison provides independent validation of the mechanistic model. Peer reviewers did not challenge this comparison, implicitly accepting it as supporting context for the mechanistic interpretation.

Both address C5-C7 core experimental approach. OpenEval finds methodology clearly described with key conclusions supported by quantitative measurements. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the methodology, stating 'integration of tmFRET with TCSPC represents an advancement' and 'data and quantitative analysis are exemplary.' OpenEval also covers C8 which peer review doesn't explicitly mention.

Partial overlap on C24-C27 TCSPC technical advantages. OpenEval finds practical benefits supported by instrument specifications and statistical theory. Peer reviewers praised the TCSPC methodology as an advancement and the quantitative analysis as exemplary, affirming these technical claims. OpenEval additionally covers C28-C30 not explicitly mentioned in peer review.
